- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) and forecast is below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overbought bias.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the peak by 5–10% to account for overreaction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive declines), apply a 3–5% downward bias to avoid lagged overcorrection.  
- If sentiment history shows a sudden shift from negative to positive (e.g., 0.3 → 0.8 in 3–5 days), increase forecast slope to match sentiment acceleration.  
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 18-day average unless sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and confirmed by multiple indicators.
